items.acceptance_excerpt: Show trends for: quality speed efficiency reliability cost success rate benchmark score Similarly show DreamCo/Buddy progress over time. Graphs must use real stored run results.

items.title: TIMEFRAME ESTIMATION
items.acceptance_excerpt: The owner wants estimates for closing benchmark gaps. Do not invent precision. Estimate using: historical rate of improvement benchmark difficulty task count available compute model cost unresolved blockers Show uncertainty.

items.title: PRODUCTION HEALTH
items.acceptance_excerpt: Dashboard should distinguish: Repository Health CI Health Runtime Health Provider Health Security Health Benchmark Health Deployment Health Customer Health A green repository build does not imply all categories are green.

items.title: RELEASE GATES
items.acceptance_excerpt: Before deployment: CODE → UNIT TESTS → INTEGRATION → SECURITY → BENCHMARKS → REGRESSION → BUILD → STAGING → E2E → RELEASE APPROVAL → PRODUCTION → POST-DEPLOY VERIFICATION

items.title: FAILURE DATABASE
items.acceptance_excerpt: Every meaningful failure should become structured learning evidence. Capture: error class environment stack trace affected capability root cause attempted repairs successful repair regression test recurrence Buddy can use historical fixes to choose repair strategies.

items.title: MODEL DRIFT
items.acceptance_excerpt: Track performance changes over time. If provider/model behavior changes: detect benchmark degradation flag drift rerun critical benchmarks adjust routing log evidence

items.title: PROVIDER OUTAGES
items.acceptance_excerpt: Design graceful failover. Provider call: primary → retry → fallback → local model when appropriate → queue/defer User should see degraded state. Do not silently produce lower-quality output without logging provider fallback.

items.title: INTERNET / NETWORK RECOVERY
items.acceptance_excerpt: Tasks should survive transient connection failures. Use: job persistence retry queues resume tokens/checkpoints idempotency backoff

items.title: DATABASE RECOVERY
items.acceptance_excerpt: Implement: migrations backup strategy transactional writes data validation restore testing Customer systems require tenant-safe recovery.

items.title: CUSTOMER SECURITY
items.acceptance_excerpt: Customer instances require isolation. Do not let: Customer A read: Customer B. Enforce boundaries in: DB filesystem secrets vector store logs task engine provider connections

items.title: DREAMCO MARKETPLACE
items.acceptance_excerpt: Long-term marketplace may allow: bots capability packs templates workflows plugins benchmark packs learning packs Each requires: publisher permissions version license security review dependencies compatibility ratings/evidence

items.title: VERSIONING
items.acceptance_excerpt: Version: Buddy capability schemas bot manifests plugins API benchmarks datasets Maintain migration compatibility.

items.title: FEATURE FLAGS
items.acceptance_excerpt: Use feature flags for experimental systems. Do not deploy unfinished experimental capabilities globally.

items.title: ACCESSIBILITY
items.acceptance_excerpt: GitHub Pages and apps should support: keyboard navigation semantic HTML labels screen readers contrast focus states Add automated checks where practical.

items.title: PERFORMANCE
items.acceptance_excerpt: Measure: page load API latency bot startup model response benchmark duration database queries memory CPU Optimize based on profiling.

items.title: TEST PYRAMID
items.acceptance_excerpt: Use: UNIT TESTS for logic. INTEGRATION TESTS for components. E2E for user workflows. BENCHMARKS for capability quality. PRODUCTION CHECKS for deployed health. Do not substitute one layer for another.

items.title: GITHUB ACTIONS RESOURCE EFFICIENCY
items.acceptance_excerpt: The owner wants maximum parallelism but also lower cost. Use: matrix builds where justified concurrency groups cache dependencies skip irrelevant workflows based on paths shard benchmark jobs artifact reuse resumable queues Do not launch 500 simultaneous expensive API jobs blindl

items.title: 24-HOUR CAPABILITY IMPROVEMENT
items.acceptance_excerpt: The owner's vision is for every hour of available compute to contribute intelligently. Prioritization: Priority = business impact × capability gap × benchmark importance × probability of improvement ÷ compute cost ÷ risk Use a real scoring implementation.

items.title: EVIDENCE FILES
items.acceptance_excerpt: Use evidence directories such as: `evidence/` or existing repository conventions. Evidence should be immutable where practical. Record: timestamp git SHA environment command benchmark version model/provider results

items.title: SOURCE PROVENANCE
items.acceptance_excerpt: Every automatically learned fact/resource should know where it came from. Store: source URL retrieval date license author/publisher content hash allowed use

items.title: RAG
items.acceptance_excerpt: Retrieval should be evidence-aware. Pipeline: QUERY → ontology → source selection → retrieve → rerank → verify source → context → model → citations → confidence

items.title: BUDDY MEMORY VS RAG
items.acceptance_excerpt: Do not confuse them. Memory = persistent context learned/stored for authorized workspace use. RAG = retrieval of sources for a current task. Both require provenance.

items.title: `buddy doctor`
items.acceptance_excerpt: This should become a powerful local troubleshooting command. Check: Python Node package managers Git repository remote branch dependencies environment required variables provider configuration frontend build backend tests database GitHub Pages deployments Never display secret val

items.title: GIT SAFETY
items.acceptance_excerpt: Before modifying repository: `git status` Confirm repository root. Confirm remote. Confirm branch. Protect uncommitted work. Never discard owner files. If dirty working tree contains unrelated edits: preserve them. Use stash only safely and intentionally.

items.title: CODEX WORKFLOW ON THE OWNER'S MAC
items.acceptance_excerpt: When running through Codex with CLI access: 1. locate Dreamcobots 2. run `pwd` 3. run `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` 4. run `git remote -v` 5. run `git status` 6. verify remote targets `DreamCo-Technologies/Dreamcobots` 7. fetch latest `main` 8. inspect repository 9. create feat

items.title: GITHUB REMOTE SAFETY
items.acceptance_excerpt: Expected primary remote should resemble: `https://github.com/DreamCo-Technologies/Dreamcobots.git` or equivalent SSH URL. Do not silently rewrite remote unless authorized.

items.title: REPOSITORY COMPARISON
items.acceptance_excerpt: When comparing old DreamCo repos with primary: Generate capability diff. For each old feature: source repository source path capability exists in primary? better/worse? conflicts? dependencies? recommended action Actions: already integrated port refactor then port archive reject

items.title: WEBSITE DEPLOYMENT TARGET
items.acceptance_excerpt: GitHub Pages should work even if backend APIs are unavailable. Static sections should still display last generated state. Dynamic actions should show: "Backend unavailable" rather than breaking the site.

items.title: OFFLINE BUDDY
items.acceptance_excerpt: Offline mode should support where possible: local knowledge local models local repository local tasks local benchmarks local file analysis Cloud-only integrations should degrade gracefully.

items.title: AI SAFETY AND HUMAN CONTROL
items.acceptance_excerpt: Buddy should be highly capable but controllable. Always preserve: explicit permissions stop controls audit logs rollback limited scopes transparent actions Capabilities should expand faster than authority.

items.title: LEGAL / COMPLIANCE
items.acceptance_excerpt: DreamCo spans regulated domains. Design capability-specific restrictions for: healthcare legal finance payments employment housing government children personal data Do not give automated agents unrestricted decision-making authority in regulated high-impact areas.

items.title: SECURITY COUNCIL
items.acceptance_excerpt: Security-critical code should trigger stronger review. Examples: authentication authorization command execution filesystem deployments customer provisioning payment code secrets public APIs Require: security review tests attack scenarios.

items.title: CHAOS / RESILIENCE TESTING
items.acceptance_excerpt: Eventually test: provider down DB unavailable network timeout invalid model output corrupted cache GitHub API failure deployment failure missing secret stale benchmark task interrupted Verify system recovers safely.

items.title: MODEL RESPONSE VALIDATION
items.acceptance_excerpt: AI output must be treated as untrusted. For structured results: schema validate sanitize reject invalid output retry or repair log failure For generated code: static analysis tests sandbox

items.title: CODE GENERATION PIPELINE
items.acceptance_excerpt: Prompt → requirements → architecture context → code → format → lint → type check → test → security → benchmark if capability-relevant → diff review → PR Never automatically deploy untested generated code.

items.title: USER FILE LEARNING
items.acceptance_excerpt: Users may provide files for Buddy. Use files for: retrieval analysis workspace learning benchmark training where explicitly authorized Track ownership and consent. Do not automatically add user data to global DreamCo training datasets.

items.title: BUSINESS DATA
items.acceptance_excerpt: Business customers may connect: CRM analytics documents databases websites payments Use the minimum permissions required.

items.title: CUSTOMER UPDATE SYSTEM
items.acceptance_excerpt: Base Buddy improvements should propagate safely. Potential: DreamCo Base → versioned releases → customer update channel → migration → tests → rollout Never overwrite: customer branding customer secrets customer data custom workflows

items.title: CUSTOMER REPOSITORY PROVISIONING
items.acceptance_excerpt: If using GitHub: create repo only after customer authorization. Prefer GitHub App / OAuth with minimum scopes. Do not use DreamCo owner's personal token for all customers.

items.title: SECRET MANAGEMENT
items.acceptance_excerpt: Support: environment variables GitHub Actions Secrets cloud secret managers local keychain Never log secret values. Never store `.env` containing real secrets in Git.

items.title: AUDIT LOG
items.acceptance_excerpt: Record sensitive actions: command user bot timestamp reason target permission result Allow review.

items.title: OWNER DASHBOARD
items.acceptance_excerpt: Owner should see: system state costs customers revenue tasks failures security deployments model usage benchmarks branch status Actions

items.title: CUSTOMER DASHBOARD
items.acceptance_excerpt: Customer should see only their tenant: Buddy tasks capabilities usage integrations data automations billing settings Never expose DreamCo internal operational dashboards.

items.title: BUDDY BIT / INSTANCE CONCEPT
items.acceptance_excerpt: Historical idea: Each customer gets their own "Buddy bit" or Buddy instance. Maintain the concept through isolated tenant deployments while sharing reusable platform code.

items.title: BUDDY MARKET POSITION
items.acceptance_excerpt: Buddy's differentiation should come from: orchestration multi-model routing evidence benchmarking capability learning business workflows local/cloud hybrid execution customer ownership bot/division organization automated software building training ground transparent progress Not

items.title: AGENT REGISTRY
items.acceptance_excerpt: Every agent/bot should register: ID name division parent capabilities tools models permissions entrypoint health check tests benchmarks status Validate registry in CI.

items.title: DYNAMIC BOT FACTORY
items.acceptance_excerpt: Earlier work reportedly moved toward dynamic generation/factories for many bots. Inspect current implementation. Use dynamic factories only where they reduce duplicate code while preserving unique bot identity.

items.title: BASE BOT FRAMEWORK
items.acceptance_excerpt: Potential historical file: `framework/base_bot.py` Verify current implementation. Base bot may provide: ID task handling logging permissions model selection tool usage health evidence memory tests Avoid God classes. Use composition.

items.title: OBSERVABILITY FIELDS
items.acceptance_excerpt: Every execution should ideally record: task ID bot ID division model provider tools start time end time latency tokens cost outcome error evidence

items.title: AI COST EXPLOSION PROTECTION
items.acceptance_excerpt: Prior DreamCo risk reviews identified cost explosion as a major concern. Implement hard safeguards before high-volume autonomous learning. No unlimited API loops.

items.title: MODEL DRIFT PROTECTION
items.acceptance_excerpt: Previous risk reviews also identified model drift. Schedule periodic critical benchmark reruns.

items.title: INFINITE LOOP PROTECTION
items.acceptance_excerpt: Prior risk reviews identified infinite loops. Hard execution ceilings are mandatory.

items.title: SECURITY RISK
items.acceptance_excerpt: Security was previously considered one of the highest project risks. Treat security code as a release blocker when critical.

items.title: REVENUE LEAKAGE
items.acceptance_excerpt: Track operating costs against realized revenue. Avoid spending more on model calls than workflows generate.

items.title: AUTH / API / RUNTIME FAILURES
items.acceptance_excerpt: Previous dashboards mentioned issues including: auth errors API failures runtime crashes logic bugs Create explicit categories and trends. Do not assume these historical problems are still active without verifying current repo.

items.title: DREAMCO LITE
items.acceptance_excerpt: Historic MVP concept: DreamCo Lite Money Bot Debug Bot one UI Do not delete this history. Determine whether capabilities graduated into current architecture. Use as reference for keeping workflows simple and executable.

items.title: LEAD GENERATION MVP
items.acceptance_excerpt: Historical MVP: LeadGenBot with: lead database CSV email copy Preserve/modernize if useful. Revenue workflows should have measurable conversion stages.

items.title: FORMULA VAULT / LEARNING MATRIX
items.acceptance_excerpt: Old UI concepts can be repurposed. Formula Vault: store reusable business/technical strategies with evidence. Learning Matrix: map: capability × resources × benchmark × bot × score.

items.title: TIME CAPSULE
items.acceptance_excerpt: Historical Time Capsule concept can become: version timeline milestone history benchmark history model changes major releases

items.title: COST TRACKING
items.acceptance_excerpt: Track: provider spend workflow cost customer cost benchmark cost division cost task cost Use real provider usage where available.

items.title: CONNECTIONS PAGE
items.acceptance_excerpt: Show authorized external systems. For each: name connection state scopes health last sync actions allowed Never imply connection merely because integration code exists.

items.title: LOANS / DEALS
items.acceptance_excerpt: Finance-related tools should be analysis tools unless properly licensed. Do not promise loan approval. Do not make unauthorized credit decisions.

items.title: LEGAL TOOLS
items.acceptance_excerpt: DreamLegal can support: legal research document analysis citations issue spotting workflow organization Do not impersonate a licensed lawyer.

items.title: HEALTH TOOLS
items.acceptance_excerpt: DreamHealth can support educational/organizational workflows. High-risk medical decisions need appropriate safeguards.

items.title: CYBERSECURITY
items.acceptance_excerpt: DreamCyber should focus on defensive authorized security. Capabilities may include: dependency scans source scans configuration validation SBOM threat modeling secrets detection secure coding No unauthorized attacks.

items.title: CRYPTO
items.acceptance_excerpt: DreamCrypto can provide: blockchain data research portfolio analytics educational simulations smart contract analysis No guaranteed returns.

items.title: MARKETPLACE
items.acceptance_excerpt: Marketplace integrations need user consent. Avoid unauthorized automation against platform terms.

items.title: SALES PROSPECTING
items.acceptance_excerpt: Sales automation should prioritize: local businesses qualified leads personalized legitimate outreach cost-saving analysis Avoid spam.

items.title: WEBSITE LINKS
items.acceptance_excerpt: Every page should use canonical paths. Create an automated route manifest. E2E tests compare rendered links against manifest.

items.title: STATIC DATA VERSIONING
items.acceptance_excerpt: GitHub Pages generated datasets should include: generation timestamp git SHA schema version

items.title: COMMAND CENTER SEARCH
items.acceptance_excerpt: Implement search across: bots capabilities divisions benchmarks models providers docs issues branches Prefer client-side indexed static search on Pages.

items.title: COMMAND PALETTE
items.acceptance_excerpt: Potential commands: Open Buddy Search bot Run benchmark Show failures Show Actions Show production blockers Open division Show model ranking Show costs

items.title: ROADMAP FROM REAL WORK
items.acceptance_excerpt: Build roadmap dynamically from: open issues failed tests benchmark gaps missing capabilities production gates dependencies Do not maintain disconnected roadmap copies.

items.title: PRIORITY ENGINE
items.acceptance_excerpt: Rank tasks using factors such as: production blocker security user impact revenue impact benchmark gap dependency count effort confidence

items.title: TASK DEPENDENCY GRAPH
items.acceptance_excerpt: Show why work is blocked. Example: Deploy Buddy Desktop blocked by: local backend verification and: secure credential storage.

items.title: BENCHMARK GAP CLOSURE
items.acceptance_excerpt: For every failed benchmark: failure → analyze → classify → select learning strategy → identify resources → practice → rerun → compare → store evidence.

items.title: USER TRAINING MODE
items.acceptance_excerpt: Buddy Bootcamp should eventually let users train themselves as well as their bots. Example: Choose Python debugging → lesson → task → sandbox → test → feedback → score.

items.title: BENCHMARK MARKETPLACE
items.acceptance_excerpt: Future concept: third parties can publish benchmark packs. Need: signed metadata version provenance safe execution scoring code review

items.title: SANDBOX
items.acceptance_excerpt: Sandbox should isolate risky execution. Possible: temporary directories Docker containers restricted subprocesses local ephemeral databases Do not run untrusted generated code directly against host system without boundaries.

items.title: SANDBOX TEST FOR EVERY RESOURCE
items.acceptance_excerpt: The owner requested every learning resource deserve a sandbox test. Interpret as: Every registered resource should link to one or more practical exercises/testing methods demonstrating what capability it helps improve. It does not mean executing arbitrary books/websites as code.

items.title: SOFTWARE BUILD SANDBOX
items.acceptance_excerpt: Generated apps should run in isolated preview before deployment.

items.title: MODEL SANDBOX
items.acceptance_excerpt: Provider models should be benchmarked with controlled prompts, datasets, budgets, and output validation.

items.title: REAL USER TESTING
items.acceptance_excerpt: Dashboard should distinguish: sandbox verification from: real-user verification. Add state such as: `needs_user_validation` without replacing core evidence taxonomy.

items.title: HUMAN FEEDBACK
items.acceptance_excerpt: Capture structured feedback: task output rating reason correction Use it to improve routing and prompts. Do not automatically globally train on private customer feedback.

items.title: BUSINESS FEEDBACK LOOP
items.acceptance_excerpt: For revenue workflows: campaign → result → conversion → analyze → adjust.

items.title: BENCHMARK SUCCESS GRAPH
items.acceptance_excerpt: Create dashboard graph showing progress over time. Dimensions: passed failed pending regression score improvement

items.title: CAPABILITY COVERAGE GRAPH
items.acceptance_excerpt: Show: catalogued implemented sandbox benchmark production.

items.title: BOT HEALTH GRAPH
items.acceptance_excerpt: Show bot health by division.

items.title: MODEL COMPARISON GRAPH
items.acceptance_excerpt: Show model: quality vs latency vs cost.

items.title: OPEN SOURCE VS CLOSED SOURCE
items.acceptance_excerpt: Track how close local/open models are to frontier providers by benchmark category. Do not use one single meaningless "AGI percentage." Use category scores.

items.title: BUDDY VS FRONTIER MODELS
items.acceptance_excerpt: Benchmark Buddy's system-level performance against models for tasks where orchestration provides value. Examples: coding workflow research tool-use workflow business launch plan debugging multi-step automation Distinguish: model intelligence from: Buddy orchestration system capab

items.title: BUDDY VALUE
items.acceptance_excerpt: Buddy can outperform a single model workflow through: model routing tools memory specialized bots multiple passes verification benchmarks recovery Measure it.

items.title: TEST DATA
items.acceptance_excerpt: Use deterministic fixtures whenever possible. Do not depend on live expensive APIs for every unit test. Have: mock tests plus: optional live provider integration tests.

items.title: LIVE PROVIDER TESTS
items.acceptance_excerpt: Live tests require secrets and should be: explicitly tagged budget capped limited non-destructive

items.title: MODEL PROVIDER HEALTH
items.acceptance_excerpt: Health statuses: configured unavailable degraded healthy rate-limited misconfigured

items.title: NETWORK STATUS
items.acceptance_excerpt: Dashboard can show: GitHub OpenAI Cloud deployment database local worker but only when real health data exists.

items.title: LOCAL WORKER
items.acceptance_excerpt: Build optional local worker architecture: Cloud queue → authorized local Buddy worker → sandbox → result upload. Do not expose user's laptop directly to public internet without secure authenticated architecture.

items.title: COMPUTER ACCESS
items.acceptance_excerpt: When Buddy has authorized local CLI access, use it for: inspection development tests builds Respect filesystem boundaries.

items.title: GITHUB APP / TOKEN SCOPES
items.acceptance_excerpt: Use minimum required scopes. For repository write access: contents write pull requests only where actually needed. Do not ask for organization-wide admin unless required.

items.title: PR TEMPLATE
items.acceptance_excerpt: PR should include: WHAT CHANGED WHY FILES TESTS RUN TEST RESULTS BENCHMARKS SECURITY KNOWN LIMITATIONS EVIDENCE NEXT STEPS

items.title: ISSUE GENERATION
items.acceptance_excerpt: Buddy may create issues for unresolved blockers. Avoid duplicate issues. Search first.

items.title: SELF-GENERATED TASKS
items.acceptance_excerpt: Buddy may generate technical maintenance tasks from evidence. Examples: failing dependency benchmark regression stale provider broken page But high-impact modifications follow approval policy.

items.title: AUTO-REPAIR BRANCH
items.acceptance_excerpt: For automated repair: `buddy/repair-<issue-id>` Run tests. Open PR. Do not self-merge production-critical fixes unless explicitly authorized by policy.

items.title: CODE REVIEW
items.acceptance_excerpt: Buddy's code-review system should inspect: correctness tests security performance architecture regressions dependency changes secrets generated artifacts

items.title: ACTIONS CODE REVIEW UI
items.acceptance_excerpt: Actions dashboard can show: PR → risk → test status → security → benchmark impact → recommended decision.

items.title: DOCUMENTATION INDEX
items.acceptance_excerpt: Parse existing `.md` files. Classify as: architecture plan capability bot division integration benchmark historical setup obsolete candidate Do not delete them automatically.

items.title: OBSOLETE DOCUMENT HANDLING
items.acceptance_excerpt: If document is obsolete: mark superseded. Link replacement. Preserve history.

items.title: REPOSITORY CLEANUP
items.acceptance_excerpt: Cleanup should focus on: generated junk caches accidental binaries duplicated dependency files broken generated artifacts dead code proven unreachable Not historical knowledge.

items.title: MIGRATION REPORT
items.acceptance_excerpt: If moving or consolidating code, record: old path → new path → compatibility layer → tests.

items.title: BACKWARDS COMPATIBILITY
items.acceptance_excerpt: Existing imports may depend on old paths. Use transition aliases when necessary.

items.title: ARCHITECTURE PRINCIPLE
items.acceptance_excerpt: Avoid both extremes: 1. thousands of isolated scripts with duplicate logic and 2. one giant monolithic Buddy file. Use modular domain architecture.

items.title: MODEL ADAPTER INTERFACE
items.acceptance_excerpt: Example conceptual API: `generate()` `stream()` `health()` `estimate_cost()` `capabilities()` `embed()` `vision()` depending on provider.

items.title: TOOL ADAPTER INTERFACE
items.acceptance_excerpt: Example: `execute(request, permissions)` `health()` `capabilities()` `cost()` `audit_metadata()`.

items.title: CAPABILITY RESOLVER
items.acceptance_excerpt: Given: "Build me a website" resolve: requirements analysis copywriting HTML/CSS/JS image generation accessibility testing deployment Then route appropriate bots/tools/models.

items.title: PLANNER
items.acceptance_excerpt: Planner should produce executable DAG when useful. Do not overplan trivial tasks.

items.title: EXECUTION ENGINE
items.acceptance_excerpt: Each task step must know: input output tool timeout retry evidence dependencies

items.title: TASK CANCELLATION
items.acceptance_excerpt: Allow user to stop long-running jobs.

items.title: TASK RESUME
items.acceptance_excerpt: Long jobs should resume from checkpoint.

items.title: IDEMPOTENCY
items.acceptance_excerpt: Repeated workflow execution should not create duplicate customer repos, payments, issues, or artifacts.

items.title: RATE LIMITING
items.acceptance_excerpt: Rate limit: APIs customer tasks provider calls GitHub writes expensive workflows.

items.title: QUEUE
items.acceptance_excerpt: Use a queue abstraction for asynchronous work. Possible backends later: database Redis cloud queue Start with simplest reliable architecture.

items.title: EVENT SYSTEM
items.acceptance_excerpt: Useful events: task\_created task\_started task\_failed task\_completed benchmark\_failed benchmark\_passed provider\_down deployment\_failed capability\_promoted

items.title: NOTIFICATIONS
items.acceptance_excerpt: Eventually support: dashboard email Slack push Use explicit opt-in.

items.title: BUSINESS AUTOMATION
items.acceptance_excerpt: Buddy may eventually support: scheduling CRM updates invoices reports marketing customer follow-ups inventory analytics Every integration requires explicit permissions.

items.title: CUSTOMER CONFIGURATION
items.acceptance_excerpt: Tenant configuration may include: company name Buddy name branding industries enabled divisions integrations data policies autonomy level budgets.

items.title: PLANS / TIERS
items.acceptance_excerpt: Capability entitlement must happen server-side. Do not rely solely on hiding UI buttons.

items.title: BILLING
items.acceptance_excerpt: Billing state should control provisioning safely. No account deletion immediately on payment failure. Use grace periods/configuration.

items.title: SELF-HOSTING
items.acceptance_excerpt: Enterprise customers may eventually self-host. Design separation between: core engine and: cloud control plane where feasible.

items.title: API CLIENTS
items.acceptance_excerpt: Keep frontend separate from provider credentials. Browser should talk to DreamCo backend. Backend talks to external providers.

items.title: CACHE
items.acceptance_excerpt: Use caching for: model metadata resource metadata benchmark definitions expensive research Invalidate intentionally.

items.title: WEB RESEARCH FRESHNESS
items.acceptance_excerpt: Track retrieval timestamps. Time-sensitive data gets expiration.

items.title: DATA QUALITY
items.acceptance_excerpt: Scoring may include: source authority agreement age completeness.

items.title: UNCERTAINTY
items.acceptance_excerpt: Buddy should be able to say: confirmed probable uncertain conflicting sources Instead of inventing confidence.

items.title: TRUST SYSTEM
items.acceptance_excerpt: Every important claim in dashboards should ideally trace back to evidence. This is core to DreamCo's differentiation.

items.title: PROJECT SUCCESS METRICS
items.acceptance_excerpt: Measure: task success benchmark improvements successful deployments customer retention workflow reliability cost per task repair success recovery time capability coverage production verification count revenue attributed to workflows

items.title: AGI-STYLE UX WITHOUT FALSE CLAIMS
items.acceptance_excerpt: The UI can feel highly intelligent by showing: planning routing memory actions learning self-repair evidence autonomy controls Do not label it AGI without legitimate scientific evidence.

items.acceptance_excerpt: During implementation provide concise progress summaries. Example: IMPLEMENTED route crawler SANDBOX VERIFIED 42/42 routes BLOCKED 3 actions require backend auth NEXT wire dispatch endpoint. Never give only generic "working on it."

Then inspect: ```bash find . -maxdepth 2 -type f | sort | head -30

items.title: TEST BASELINE FIRST
items.acceptance_excerpt: Before changing code, capture baseline: test command test count failures Actions state frontend build backend build Store evidence.

items.title: CREATE FEATURE BRANCH
items.acceptance_excerpt: Use descriptive branch such as: `codex/command-center-production-repair` or a smaller scope based on first validated problem.

items.title: REPAIR BEFORE EXPANDING
items.acceptance_excerpt: If core CI is broken, repair that first. Do not add hundreds of new features onto a broken baseline.

items.title: GITHUB PAGES FIRST VERTICAL SLICE
items.acceptance_excerpt: A high-value early milestone: GitHub Pages successfully loads deterministic real repository status. Implement: repository inventory generator → JSON → dashboard → E2E test → Actions workflow → evidence. This creates the foundation for every future dashboard.

items.title: FIRST BENCHMARK VERTICAL SLICE
items.acceptance_excerpt: Prove: one real capability → benchmark → failure → learning recommendation → rerun → stored evidence before scaling to 500.

items.title: FIRST BOT PROSPECTUS VERTICAL SLICE
items.acceptance_excerpt: Generate bot dashboard automatically from live registry. Then prove generator supports every registered bot.

items.title: FIRST DIVISION VERTICAL SLICE
items.acceptance_excerpt: Generate one division page. Then generalize across all divisions.

items.title: FIRST MODEL LAB VERTICAL SLICE
items.acceptance_excerpt: Register several real providers/models with: canonical IDs metadata health benchmark interface Then scale registry.

items.title: OPENAI TEST
items.acceptance_excerpt: If `OPENAI_API_KEY` exists in GitHub Actions: create a minimal budget-capped integration health workflow if one does not already exist. Do NOT print the key. Test real request. Validate result. Store non-sensitive evidence.

items.title: USER-FACING CAPABILITY BUTTONS
items.acceptance_excerpt: Capability test buttons should either: A. launch a secure real test or B. link to latest real evidence. Never simulate success.

items.title: CODEX SHOULD USE THE LOCAL COMPUTER
items.acceptance_excerpt: When authorized CLI access is available, actively use it. Do not make the owner copy-paste dozens of commands you can execute yourself. Inspect. Build. Test. Commit. Push branch. Open PR.

items.title: NEVER PRETEND A PUSH OCCURRED
items.acceptance_excerpt: Only say code was pushed after: `git push` succeeds. Only say a PR exists if GitHub confirms it. Only say Actions passed if actual workflow results confirm it.

items.title: MAIN REPOSITORY IS PRIORITY
items.acceptance_excerpt: Do not accidentally perform primary work in: `ireanjordan24/dreamcobots` if the intended repository is: `DreamCo-Technologies/Dreamcobots`. Use old repositories primarily for capability comparison and historical recovery unless instructed otherwise.

items.title: DREAMCO SHOULD RUN AS ONE FULL SYSTEM
items.acceptance_excerpt: A major requirement is merging disconnected historical systems into a coherent operating system. This does NOT require physically merging everything into one file. It means: shared registries shared task engine shared ontology shared evidence shared dashboard shared benchmark eng

items.title: EVERYTHING SHOULD BE TRACEABLE
items.acceptance_excerpt: A user should be able to click: Capability and see: bot division code test benchmark learning resources workflow deployment production evidence. Likewise clicking a bot should expose its whole chain.

items.title: FUTURE DREAMCO GOAL
items.acceptance_excerpt: DreamCo's long-term goal is to become an autonomous, evidence-driven operating platform capable of helping a user go from: IDEA to: WORKING COMPANY / PRODUCT / SYSTEM. It should combine: AI software automation business strategy model routing learning research deployment customer

items.title: DEFINITION OF DONE FOR EACH PR
items.acceptance_excerpt: A PR is done only when: code exists code is understandable tests exist tests actually ran security reviewed generated data validates documentation updated where necessary no unrelated functionality removed no secrets exposed evidence included limitations listed

items.title: CODE QUALITY
items.acceptance_excerpt: Prefer: typed code small modules meaningful names clear interfaces deterministic behavior testability dependency injection explicit errors Avoid: 5,000-line modules excessive global state hardcoded secrets impossible-to-test singletons silent exception swallowing fake mocks in pr

items.title: FAILURE HONESTY
items.acceptance_excerpt: If something fails, say: FAILED and include the failure. If partially working: PARTIAL. If blocked: BLOCKED. This system's credibility depends on truthful evidence.

items.title: NO CAPABILITY LOSS
items.acceptance_excerpt: When consolidating old bots into superbots/master bots: count capabilities before and after. New system must preserve or expand unique capabilities. Generate a capability migration report.

items.title: OLD BOT IMPORT
items.acceptance_excerpt: Create tooling to parse historical bot specifications and map them into modern bot manifests where feasible. Never manually recreate thousands of entries.

items.title: REGISTRY VALIDATION
items.acceptance_excerpt: CI should reject: duplicate bot IDs duplicate benchmark IDs duplicate resource IDs missing division missing capability links invalid source paths invalid status transitions.

items.title: STATUS TRANSITIONS
items.acceptance_excerpt: Allowed: catalogued → implemented implemented → sandbox\_verified sandbox\_verified → benchmark\_verified benchmark\_verified → regression\_verified regression\_verified → production\_verified If regression occurs, retain history and mark current regression. Do not erase previous

items.title: BENCHMARK EVIDENCE IMMUTABILITY
items.acceptance_excerpt: Never rewrite historical benchmark results to make graphs look better. New run = new record.

items.title: CUSTOMER DATA POLICIES
items.acceptance_excerpt: Customer chooses where possible: local only DreamCo cloud customer cloud hybrid.

items.title: PRIVACY-FIRST DEFAULT
items.acceptance_excerpt: Collect only necessary information. Do not collect data merely because future AI might use it.

items.title: API RATE / COST ESTIMATION
items.acceptance_excerpt: Before large benchmark batches: estimate: calls tokens provider cost runtime. Require budget guard.

items.title: LOCAL-FIRST BENCHMARKS
items.acceptance_excerpt: Use local/open models for appropriate practice and cheap baseline evaluation. Use frontier APIs for targeted comparisons.

items.title: MULTI-MODEL COUNCIL COST POLICY
items.acceptance_excerpt: Council size should vary: simple task → 1 model medium → 2-3 high stakes/complex → council.

items.title: BENCHMARK REPRODUCIBILITY
items.acceptance_excerpt: Record: prompt dataset version model version where available temperature seed where available evaluator scoring version.

items.title: LLM-AS-JUDGE
items.acceptance_excerpt: If using LLM judges: use rubric calibrate consider multiple judges for important benchmarks include deterministic validation where possible never rely solely on self-grading.

items.title: WEBSITE QUALITY BENCHMARKS
items.acceptance_excerpt: For web capability: HTML validity accessibility responsive behavior broken links performance content requirements visual checks where possible.

items.title: CODING BENCHMARKS
items.acceptance_excerpt: Use: unit tests hidden tests where applicable lint typing security performance rather than subjective "looks correct."

items.title: BUSINESS BENCHMARKS
items.acceptance_excerpt: Use measurable outputs where possible: completeness source quality financial consistency customer relevance legal caveats.

items.title: RESEARCH BENCHMARKS
items.acceptance_excerpt: Measure: citation correctness source quality freshness claim support contradiction detection hallucination.

items.title: ROUTING BENCHMARKS
items.acceptance_excerpt: Measure whether router picks the most efficient capable model/tool.

items.title: REPAIR BENCHMARKS
items.acceptance_excerpt: Measure: fault detection root-cause accuracy repair success tests passed regression rate cost.

items.title: AGENT BENCHMARKS
items.acceptance_excerpt: Measure: planning task completion tool correctness recovery unnecessary steps cost.

items.title: REVENUE BENCHMARKS
items.acceptance_excerpt: Measure workflow execution quality, not guaranteed dollars.

items.title: LATENCY
items.acceptance_excerpt: Record P50/P95 where enough samples exist.

items.title: RELIABILITY
items.acceptance_excerpt: Track successful completions / attempts.

items.title: COST
items.acceptance_excerpt: Provider pricing changes. Store pricing version/timestamp.

items.title: GITHUB ACTION HISTORY
items.acceptance_excerpt: Command Center should ingest real run histories when APIs allow. Do not fabricate missing logs.

items.title: ISSUE INTELLIGENCE
items.acceptance_excerpt: Buddy should connect recurring failures to issues.

items.title: CODE OWNER / REVIEW RULES
items.acceptance_excerpt: High-risk modules can require designated review.

items.title: SECURITY TESTS
items.acceptance_excerpt: Include: secret leakage path traversal unauthorized command invalid token role bypass tenant isolation.

items.title: BROWSER SECURITY
items.acceptance_excerpt: Never expose API secret through bundled frontend environment variables.

items.title: CONTENT SECURITY POLICY
items.acceptance_excerpt: Add CSP where appropriate.

items.title: DEPLOYMENT SECRETS
items.acceptance_excerpt: Use platform secret managers.

items.title: SBOM
items.acceptance_excerpt: Generate software bill of materials for production releases where practical.

items.title: LICENSE SCAN
items.acceptance_excerpt: Track third-party package licenses. Important because DreamCo may become commercial.

items.title: USER RIGHTS
items.acceptance_excerpt: Support data export/deletion where applicable.

items.title: BACKUP
items.acceptance_excerpt: Test restore. Backup existing does not prove recovery.

items.title: ROLLBACK
items.acceptance_excerpt: Deployments need known previous version.

items.title: RELEASE NOTES
items.acceptance_excerpt: Generate from actual PRs/commits.

items.title: DREAMCO AS A PLATFORM
items.acceptance_excerpt: Long-term architecture should support: Core Buddy capability modules model providers plugins bots marketplace customer workspaces without forking the entire codebase for every customer.

items.title: CUSTOMER CUSTOMIZATION
items.acceptance_excerpt: Allow customer to rename Buddy and customize interface without changing core.

items.title: CUSTOMER EXTENSIONS
items.acceptance_excerpt: Customers may install their own tools/plugins under policy.

items.title: ENTERPRISE
items.acceptance_excerpt: Future enterprise requirements: SSO audit logs RBAC private deployment retention admin dashboard. Don't prematurely implement all unless dependencies warrant.

items.title: RBAC
items.acceptance_excerpt: Roles may include: owner admin developer operator member viewer Permissions explicit.

items.title: BUDGET POLICY
items.acceptance_excerpt: Per-user, per-customer, per-provider budgets.

items.title: EMERGENCY STOP
items.acceptance_excerpt: Owner can stop: agents provider spending deployments local commands customer automation.

items.title: SAFE MODE
items.acceptance_excerpt: Provide safe/degraded mode where external side effects are disabled.

items.title: AUDITABILITY
items.acceptance_excerpt: The owner should always be able to answer: "What did Buddy do?"

items.title: END GOAL FOR CODEX
items.acceptance_excerpt: Do not attempt to implement all 300+ directives in one destructive mega-commit. This document defines the complete north star and constraints. Work continuously through the dependency graph. For every session: 1. inspect actual state 2. choose the highest-value executable blocker

items.title: START NOW
items.acceptance_excerpt: First verify the local repository and remote. Then inspect the live repository architecture. Then run existing tests and examine failing GitHub Actions. Then identify the highest-impact blocker preventing the existing GitHub Pages / Actions / Buddy system from operating correctly
